issues.summary: Early return on unknown decimals skips all inline amount validation (int96 range and decimal length), so bad amounts only fail later on the review step
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: CreateSpendingLimit/index.tsx:24 returns undefined when decimals is null, and validateDecimalLength (packages/utils/src/utils/validation.ts:120) also returns early for null maxLen, so nothing checks the amount. The PR intends this and names the unguarded Next click as a risk. The later failure is a generic error in createNewSpendingLimitTx, with no funds at risk, and only very large or >18-decimal amounts on a zero-balance Safe hit it.

issues.summary: Review step passes undefined decimals to createNewSpendingLimitTx, which silently defaults parseUnits to 18 decimals
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: ReviewSpendingLimit/index.tsx:33 and spendingLimitExecution.ts:99 (`tokenDecimals ?? undefined`) are unchanged by the PR. In practice only the native token (the default, almost always 18 decimals) can be missing from balances, because the selector offers only visible balances. So a wrong allowance for a 6-decimal token is theoretical.

issues.summary: Review hides SendAmountBlock when the token is missing, so the amount is not shown before signing
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: ReviewSpendingLimit/index.tsx:101 renders the amount block only when `token` is set. This code predates the PR and sits outside the diff, but zero-balance Safes can now reach review with an amount.

issues.summary: `decimals ?? 'Gwei'` fallback is now unreachable dead code
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: CreateSpendingLimit/index.tsx:24 returns when decimals == null, so at line 27 `?? 'Gwei'` can never apply and just leaves a confusing, invalid ethers v6 unit in the code.

issues.summary: Unknown-decimals test covers only '1' and '1.1', not too-large or too-many-decimals inputs
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: SpendingLimitForm.test.ts's new case asserts undefined only for '1' and '1.1'. It pins the skip but does not document what happens to out-of-range inputs, which now pass through to review.

issues.summary: Test fixture is hand-written instead of using balanceBuilder/nativeTokenBuilder
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: CreateSpendingLimit.test.tsx:21 builds nativeBalance by hand, although apps/web/src/tests/builders/balances.ts provides nativeTokenBuilder/balanceBuilder that could be overridden with ZERO_ADDRESS. This is a convention preference with no functional cost.

issues.summary: New test added to the legacy out-of-feature test file with deep import and eslint-disable instead of the new in-feature test
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: The eslint-disable deep import at SpendingLimitForm.test.ts:1 was already there. The PR only added a case to an existing describe block. Moving it would be tidier, but nothing concrete breaks.

issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: TokenAmountInput/index.tsx uses the bracket form, ui/combobox.tsx:140 uses the v4 shorthand, and navigation-menu.tsx:114 uses brackets. Both forms work, so this is purely stylistic.

issues.summary: Blank token selector on zero-balance Safe; suggest showing native currency
issues.label: wrong
issues.evidence: TokenAmountInput/index.tsx renders '' when the selected token is missing from balances. The PR description says a blank trigger is the intended behaviour, matching main's MUI behaviour. This is a UX suggestion, not a defect in the change.

issues.summary: No stated product/design sign-off for the behaviour change
issues.label: unverifiable
issues.evidence: Whether product or design approved this can't be settled from the code. The PR links a Linear ticket (WA-3452) that describes the fix.
